newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal, grain cars up sharply in year.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal, grain cars up sharply in year.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic as measured in intermodal and carloads of grain rose sharply in the week ended November 9 from the year-ago week, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said that intermodal traffic, which does not include carloads, rose 5.2 percent to 170,391 trailers and containers from 161,967 in the year-ago week. Carloads of grain rose 14.9 percent to 31,151 in the week from 27,112 a year ago.

AAR said overall carloads also rose 1.7 percent to 352,411 in the week from 346,603 a year ago. Ton-miles stood at 26.4 billion, up 2.3 percent from 25.8 billion a year ago. A ton-mile is equal to one ton of freight hauled one mile.
"This is a rather typical week with robust growth in intermodal traffic and more modest growth in carload freight," Harvey Levine, AAR chief economist, said.
"With no immediate expectations of higher interest rates, weather is the biggest single factor that could affect traffic through the end of the year," Levine said.
AAR said that other notable increases were in carloads of crushed stone, sand and gravel which rose 11.2 percent in the week to 17,168 from 15,440 in the year-ago week.
Grain mill products increased 7.7 percent in the week to 9,834 carloads from 9,127 last year, while lumber and wood products rose 8.9 percent to 5,314 from 4,880 last year, AAR said.
Stone, clay and glass products rose 7.2 percent to 10,233 carloads from 9,547 in the same 1996 week, while petroleum carloads increased 2.6 percent to 5,392 from 5,254.
But motor vehicles and parts loadings fell 2.5 percent to 19,557 carloads from 20,063 in the year-ago week.

Farm products other than grain stood at 2,459 loadings in the week, down 1.5 percent from 2,497 in the same 1995 week, while nonmetallic minerals fell 3.5 percent to 8,721 carloads from 9,033 last year.
In the first 45 weeks of 1996, AAR said ton-miles rose two percent from the same period last year. Intermodal traffic also rose 1.5 percent, but carloads fell 0.6 percent, AAR said.
